accepted.question_text: For the four-parameter orthogonal polynomial H_n(z; μ, ν, α, θ) on the real line, together with the two discrete versions that the source denotes by h_n(k; μ, ν, α, β) and g_n(k; μ, ν, β, N), can one derive a full analytic description from their current definition by three-term recursion relations and initial values alone? In particular, determine their weight functions, generating functions, asymptotics, orthogonality relations, Rodrigues-type formulas, forward/backward shift operator relations, zeros, and a closed-form representation, for example in terms of hypergeometric functions.
accepted.context_brief: First polynomial class and its discrete versions

evidence.quote: Since 2005, however, we found a new class of exactly solvable problems that are associated with orthogonal polynomials, which were overlooked in the mathematics and physics literature [5-12]. These polynomials are defined, up to now, by their three-term recursion relations and initial value P_0(ε) = 1. However, their other important properties are yet to be derived analytically. These properties include the weight functions, generating functions, asymptotics, orthogonality relations, Rodrigues-type formulas, etc.

Due to the prime significance of these new (or modified) polynomials along with their discrete versions to the solution of various problems in physics and mathematics, we urge experts in the field of orthogonal polynomials to study them, derive their analytic properties and write them in closed form (e.g., in terms of hypergeometric functions). The sought-after properties of these polynomials include the weight functions, generating functions, asymptotics, orthogonality relations, Rodrigues-type formulas, Forward/Backward shift operator relations, zeros, etc.

accepted.question_text: For the second four-parameter polynomial class Q_n(z; μ, ν, α, θ), which the source places on the real line, and for its companion version G_n(z; μ, ν, α, β), can one derive the analytic properties that are not yet available from the recursion-relation definition alone? The missing analytic information explicitly sought in the source includes weight functions, generating functions, asymptotics, orthogonality relations, Rodrigues-type formulas, forward/backward shift operator relations, zeros, and a closed-form expression such as a hypergeometric representation.
